title: Rookie Rachael Li Wins U.S. Women's Title; Wesley So Loses, Faces Caruana In Playoffs
summary: Nobody is happier after 11 rounds of the 2026 U.S. Chess Championship than GM Fabiano Caruana, who has a new chance to win his fifth consecutive title. GM Wesley So entered the final round with a full-point lead, but the most likely result was not what we saw. GM Sam Sevian outplayed So in a heavy-piece endgame, while GM Fabiano Caruana won on demand against GM Awonder Liang to force playoffs on Thursday. The top-five finishers qualify for the next FIDE World Cup. Rookie WIM Rachael Li won the 2026 U.S. Women's Chess Championship after making a draw with IM Anna Zatonskih. The 16-year-old is the youngest first-timer to win the event, and she earned $45,000, including the top prize, a $5,000 winner's bonus, and the $5,000 Finish Strong Prize. She also earned her first IM norm with two rounds to spare, in addition to a 50-point rating gain. Rachael Li and IM Alice Lee (second place) qualify for the next FIDE Women's World Cup. Final Standings | Open Final Standings | Women Round 11 Results: Open Asked in the previous round how he assessed his chances, Caruana said that there was "zero percent" chance So would lose, even if Caruana managed to somehow win on demand. After his game, of course, he revised his statement. By the time Caruana won, So was much worse in an endgame against Sevian. The American number-one and defending champion went over his full game, starting with his interesting 6.Bf4 idea in the Tarrasch Defense, a move his second, GM Grigoriy Oparin, said he'd shared in Wijk aan Zee this year. Caruana went for a kingside attack, and although the first wave of fire didn't break the barricades, he initiated a second wave with 26.Ne4!.

title: Anton, Harikrishna Give Novy Bor Crucial Win Over Alkaloid
summary: GM Nihal Sarin could afford to take a draw in a won position against GM Wei Yi as GMs David Anton and Pentala Harikrishna gave Novy Bor Chess Club a 4-2 victory over second-seed Alkaloid. In the penultimate round, they'll face the only other team on a perfect score, SuperChess Romania, who swept aside SK K CERO INVEST Nitra 5.5-0.5, with the only draw conceded by GM Nodirbek Abdusattorov against GM Vasyl Ivanchuk. It's tight at the top, with three teams within a single point of the leaders. Meanwhile, CE Gambit Bonnevoie continues to lead the 2026 European Women's Chess Club Cup with a perfect score after beating second-seed Sirmium Sremska Mitrovica 2.5-1.5. There were three wild draws, but IM Aleksandra Maltsevskaya grabbed the crucial win against IM Teodora Injac. Cercle d'Echecs de Monte-Carlo bounced back to win 4-0 and is joined by Odlar Yurdu as the only teams within two points of the leaders. Round six is on Thursday, October 22, starting at 8 a.m. ET / 14:00 CEST / 5:30 p.m. IST. The convincing win for fourth-seed Novy Bor over second-seed Alkaloid was by far the most significant result of round five, with favorites winning the other key matches. That leaves two teams in the lead going into the penultimate round, but if they tie their head-to-head clash, three teams are within a point and can catch them. 10 teams are another point back and still in the medal hunt. Open Standings After Round 5 (Top 12) The key match of the round was also the longest and most intense, with Novy Bor, the European Club Cup champions in 2013, 2022, and 2024, pulling off an impressive win. The most exciting game was perhaps Wei vs. Nihal, with the Chinese grandmaster, who had started with 4/4 in Budva, commenting: "I think today was a crazy game, because my opponent sacrificed a piece early in the opening and I think my position should be very good, but then maybe I missed some great chances to win." I think today was a crazy game! —Wei Yi Nihal was following a game he'd won with Black against GM Gukesh Dommaraju in the Menorca Open Masters rapid event earlier this year. Wei at first seemed to make the same mistake as the world champion, then was close to winning, and then, as he confessed, he lost control in a situation where he made a move with two seconds on his clock: "In time trouble. I think my opponent played much better than me and even in the final position he has some chances to score. But maybe he saw his teammates and they had good positions, so he decided to go for the draw." In fact, the final position, where a draw was agreed, is completely winning for Black.

title: Lionel Messi Shares ChatGPT Chess Lesson With 517 Million Instagram Followers
summary: Argentinian superstar Lionel Messi shared a chess-themed ad for ChatGPT with his 517 million Instagram followers on Wednesday, in a post that is bound to generate massive interest. The world's second-most followed person on Instagram, behind only Cristiano Ronaldo, is shown in a video asking for chess instructions one move at a time. Within a few hours of being posted, the video had already racked up more than a million likes and 13,000 comments. “Chat, you know my style. Show me a good chess opening, step by step,” he says in Spanish. By the end of the clip, he is ready to try another. The premise is explained in the caption. “I asked ChatGPT to teach me a chess opening that matched my style. It suggested Goat Horns.”

title: Play Chess Against NBA Star Steven Adams
summary: Think you can dunk on an NBA player at chess? Houston Rockets star Steven Adams is now a bot on Chess.com! Head to the Play Bots page and try your luck against our tallest chess bot ever! With a towering 6'11" presence and a tough chess rating of 1500, this might be the only chance you ever have of scoring on the basketball legend from New Zealand. Challenge Steven Adams A chess fan for years, in March 2026 Steven was a featured speaker at the 20th annual MIT Sloan Sports Analytics Conference. While there, he visited Chess.com’s dedicated space and had the chance to meet the Chessbrahs and IM Danny Rensch. In the summer of 2020, Steven posted a series of chess screenshots and trash-talking tweets, including an image of a smothered mate. These were aimed at fellow NBA players and the NBA itself ahead of the league’s restart in the Orlando bubble following the pandemic lockdown. Steven’s bot launch coincides with the Houston Rockets 2026-27 NBA regular season opener against the Dallas Mavericks on Wednesday, October 21. Can you beat him before the NBA season starts? title: Kazakhstan dominates World U7–U17 Championships in Roquetas de Mar
summary: With an outstanding medal haul across the age categories, Kazakhstan emerged as one of the leading forces at the 2026 World Youth Championships, showcasing the strength of its next generation of chess talent. The 2026 World U7–U17 Chess Championships came to a close in Roquetas de Mar, Spain, with a festive closing ceremony celebrating the achievements of hundreds of young players from around the world. After 11 rounds of competition, the event reached its climax as the newly crowned world champions and medallists received their awards, marking the culmination of an intense championship filled with ambition, determination, and memorable battles over the board. Hosted at the Evenia Zoraida Hotel Resort, the championship welcomed 721 players representing 82 countries. Beyond the results and medals, the event provided a meeting point for young chess talents from across the globe, united by their passion for the game. The ceremony brought together players, families, coaches, officials and representatives of the international chess community to celebrate the accomplishments of the participants across all 12 age and gender categories. Music and dance The evening opened with a vibrant music and dance performance by the Duende Andaluz flamenco group, which was warmly received by the more than 1,000 players and accompanying guests in attendance. Authorities, speeches and anthems Following the presentation of the attending authorities, Javier Ochoa de Echagüen, President of the Spanish Chess Federation, delivered a welcome address. He reminded the audience that Roquetas de Mar will remain an important destination on the international chess calendar, hosting the World Rapid and Blitz Championships in 2027, after Easter Week, as well as the World U7–U11 Championships in November. Ozgur Solakoğlu, FIDE Technical Delegate, also addressed the audience, congratulating all the young players on their achievements and commending their participation in the championship. Other distinguished guests taking part in the prize-giving ceremony included Dominic Cross, President of the Portuguese Chess Federation; Javier Rubio Doblas, President of the Andalusian Chess Federation; Miguel Álvarez Morales, Tournament Director; José Molina Guijarro, Director of the Evenia Zoraida Resort; and IA Takis Nikolopoulos, Main Arbiter. The ceremony also paid tribute to Spain and FIDE with the playing of their respective national and organisational anthems, adding a solemn and memorable touch to the celebrations. Prize-winners The Girls U7 category was dominated by Kazakhstan, with Leila Aldazharova claiming the gold medal with 9/11 and compatriot Alima Akimkhan taking silver with 8.5/11. Canada’s Echo Heming Fang also scored 8.5/11 to secure the bronze medal among the 28 participants. The title race went down to the final round, with Aldazharova and Fang both on 8/10. Aldazharova’s decisive victory over Chen Yi Estelle Yap proved crucial, while Fang could only manage a draw, allowing the Kazakh player to claim gold outright. The Open U7 category delivered an exciting finale, with decisive results on the top ten boards keeping the medal race alive until the very end. Kazakhstan’s Makar Chernyshov won his final-round game to secure the gold medal with an impressive 9/11. Poland’s Ignacy Mongay Miland and Daniil Aslanov, competing under the FIDE flag, both finished on 8.5/11, with Mongay Miland edging out his rival to claim silver, leaving Aslanov with bronze. The section featured 53 players, and Egypt’s Mohab Ahmed Assem endured a particularly disappointing final round. Starting the day among the leaders on 8/10, he suffered a defeat that pushed him down to fourth place, just outside the podium. Still, he could take some consolation in a strong tournament performance – and perhaps a few extra rating points for his digital chess résumé! The Girls U9 category, which featured 40 players, produced a closely contested finish, with three players tied on 8.5/11 after eleven rounds. Amaliya Yedresheva of Kazakhstan, Varvara Volkova competing under the FIDE flag, and Stella Zhu representing Finland shared the top score. The tiebreak criteria confirmed the final ranking, awarding the gold medal to Yedresheva, who had started the tournament as the 18th seed. Her victory added another gold medal to Kazakhstan’s growing tally at the championship, while Volkova took silver and Zhu claimed bronze. The Open U9 section, which brought together 82 players, saw Ukraine’s Myron Netrebka claim the gold medal with an outstanding 9.5/11. Uzbekistan’s Sayfuddin Erkinboev finished a half-point behind on 9/11 to take silver, while Poland’s Wiktor Stankowski secured bronze with 8.5/11. The final round proved decisive in shaping the podium. Stankowski, playing Black, defeated Erkinboev in a must-win encounter, while Netrebka converted his opportunity on the second board into a victory. The Ukrainian’s win allowed him to finish clear of the field and secure the title outright. The Girls U11 category witnessed a remarkable performance by top seed WCM Milana Filippova of Kazakhstan, who swept the field with a perfect 11/11, winning every game to claim the gold medal in emphatic fashion. Among the 47 participants, Filippova left her rivals trailing by a substantial margin. Alexandra Aymerich Sazonova, playing under the FIDE flag and seeded 20th, produced an impressive performance to secure silver with 8/11. Uzbekistan’s WFM Husnorakhon Khusnitdinova also scored 8/11 to take bronze. Filippova’s achievement was all the more remarkable given that she defeated both of her fellow medallists, who had started the tournament as the fourth and fifth seeds, respectively. A perfect score of 11 points from 11 games made her one of the standout performers of the entire championship. The Open U11 category saw a thrilling battle for the gold medal between CM Amirzhan Anetov of Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan’s Akbar Mustafakulov. With the title race finely balanced, Anetov delivered a decisive late surge, winning his final four games in a row, including a crucial victory over Mustafakulov, to secure the gold medal. Kazakhstan celebrated another podium finish as Rauan Bakhyt claimed bronze, completing a strong showing for the Central Asian chess powerhouse in a section featuring 99 players. The Girls U13 category brought together 43 players for eleven hard-fought rounds, with Uzbekistan claiming both gold and silver. WCM Lazizabonu Komiljonova emerged victorious with 8.5/11, finishing half a point ahead of compatriot WFM Sarvinoz

title: European Club Cup: Novy Bor and SuperChess remain perfect
summary:
Novy Bor and SuperChess Romania remain the only teams with perfect scores in the open section of the European Club Cup after five rounds. The co-leaders will face each other in Thursday's penultimate round, with three teams following one match point behind. In the women's competition, CE Gambit Bonnevoie secured their fifth consecutive victory and now hold a two-point lead over Monte-Carlo and Odlar Yurdu with two rounds remaining. | Pictured: SuperChess' Jorden van Foreest and Nodirbek Abdusattorov | Photo: Gerd Densing

Open: Co-leaders set for direct encounter in Thursday's penultimate round

With two rounds to go at the European Club Cup in Budva, only two teams remain on perfect scores of 10/10 match points in the open section. Fourth seeds Novy Bor Chess Club defeated second seeds Alkaloid 4–2 in Wednesday's fifth round, while defending champions SuperChess Romania secured a convincing 5½–½ victory over SK K CERO INVEST Nitra.

The two leaders will face each other in Thursday's penultimate round, with three teams following just one match point behind.

Novy Bor's victory over Alkaloid was the most significant result of the day, as the Czech club handed the North Macedonian representatives their first defeat of the tournament. The match featured two decisive games, with David Anton defeating Aravindh Chithambaram and Pentala Harikrishna overcoming Yu Yangyi. The latter victory came after 103 moves and secured the match win for Novy Bor.

On the top two boards, Nodirbek Yakubboev drew with Arjun Erigaisi, while Nihal Sarin split the point with Wei Yi. Wei had previously won all four of his games in Budva, but on this occasion he faced considerable difficulties against his Indian opponent. Nihal eventually agreed to a draw despite having a winning position, with his teammates already on course to secure the match victory. Nils Grandelius and Jonas Buhl Bjerre also drew their games, completing Novy Bor's 4–2 win.

Novy Bor obtained a crucial victory over Alkaloid | Photo: Gerd Densing

SuperChess Romania, meanwhile, ended the perfect run of twelfth seeds SK K CERO INVEST Nitra. The Romanian club collected five victories, with Jorden van Foreest, Haik Martirosyan, Alexey Sarana, Bogdan-Daniel Deac and Daniel Dardha all scoring full points. Sarana maintained his individual perfect score, reaching 5/5.

The only player to avoid defeat for Nitra was Vasyl Ivanchuk, who drew with Nodirbek Abdusattorov on the top board. The Ukrainian veteran, who has enjoyed a strong tournament so far, held the highest-rated participant in the competition to a draw with the black pieces.

Alexey Sarana (left) has a perfect 5/5 score for SuperChess | Photo: Gerd Densing

Three teams follow the co-leaders on 9/10 match points: top seeds Bayegan Pendik Chess Sports Club, fifth seeds Tuxera Aquaprofit Nagykanizsai and sixth seeds Elektroprivreda.

Bayegan Pendik recovered from their fourth-round draw against Elektroprivreda by defeating Aix-en-Provence 4½–1½. Anish Giri and Yagiz Kaan Erdogmus, who had both suffered defeats on Tuesday, drew their games this time, while victories on the bottom three boards gave the Turkish club a comfortable match win.

Tuxera Aquaprofit Nagykanizsai defeated Riehen 5½–½, while Elektroprivreda secured a 4½–1½ victory over SK Dunajska Streda. The latter match included a notable individual upset, as 16-year-old Czech grandmaster Vaclav Finek defeated Pranav Venkatesh, who had beaten Giri in the previous round. Despite Finek's victory, the remaining boards went decisively in Elektroprivreda's favour.

Bayegan Pendik Chess Sports Club defeated Aix-en-Provence on Wednesday - Volodar Murzin beat Maxime Roganova with black | Photo: Gerd Densing

TJ Slavia CAISSA Cadca (seeded 25 th , right) obtained an upset 3½-2½ victory over Vugar Gashimov (seeded 8 th , left) | Photo: Gerd Densing

The sixth round will feature the direct encounter between SuperChess Romania and Novy Bor, while Alkaloid will attempt to recover from their defeat against Elektroprivreda. With the two leaders only one match point ahead of the chasing trio, the results of Thursday's matches will be particularly important in determining the contenders for the title.

Women's: Gambit Bonnevoie win again, lead

CE Gambit Bonnevoie maintained their perfect record in the women's competition by defeating second seeds Sirmium Sremska Mitrovica 2½–1½. The Luxembourg-based club, seeded fourth, have now beaten each of the three highest-rated teams and lead the standings with 10/10 match points, two ahead of Cercle d'Echecs de Monte-Carlo and Odlar Yurdu.

Following their fourth-round victory over defending champions Monte-Carlo, Gambit Bonnevoie secured another important win thanks to Aleksandra Maltsevskaya, who defeated Teodora Injac on the fourth board. The remaining three games ended in draws, with Anna Ushenina splitting the point with Polina Shuvalova, Klaudia Kulon drawing with Leya Garifullina and Elina Danielian sharing the point with Nurgyul Salimova.

The victory leaves Gambit Bonnevoie as the only team with five wins from five matches. Having already defeated the top three seeds, the Luxembourg representatives will face fifth seeds Odlar Yurdu in Thursday's sixth round.

CE Gambit Bonnevoie: Anna Ushenina, Klaudia Kulon, Elina Danielian and Aleksandra Maltsevskaya | Photo: Gerd Densing

Monte-Carlo recovered from their fourth-round defeat with a 4–0 victory over Velikova Chess Club, the 18 th seeds. Humpy Koneru, Stavroula Tsolakidou, Elisabeth Paehtz and Pia Cramling all won their games against the Bulgarian team, who had exceeded expectations in the first four rounds. The result lifted Monte-Carlo to second place in the standings on tiebreaks.

Odlar Yurdu also reached 8/10 match points by defeating Crvena Zvezda 3–1. The Azerbaijani club conceded a point on the top board, where Ulviyya Fataliyeva lost to Alina Bivol, but Gunay Mammadzada, Khanim Balajayeva and Gulnar Mammadova all secured victories.

Third seeds SuperChess Romania moved into fourth place with 7/10 match points after beating Gambit ASEE 3½–½. Nino Batsiashvili, Deimante Daulyte-Cornette and Irina Bulmaga won their games, while Dinara Wagner drew with Beloslava Krasteva.

Pia Cramling and Elisabeth Paehtz helped Monte-Carlo recover from the loss in round four | Photo: Gerd Densing

SuperChess Romania (right) defeated Gambit ASEE | Photo: Gerd Densing

Another individual result of note came from 11-year-old English player Bodhana Sivanandan, who defeated Ena Cvitan with the black pieces. It was Sivanandan's third victory in Budva, following wins in rounds two and three and a draw against Batsiashvili in round four.

Despite Sivanandan's victory, her team, She Plays To Win Lionesses A, suffered a 2½–1½ defeat against Zenski Sahovski Klub Napredak Zenica. The English representatives remain on 3/10 match points, while Sivanandan has continued to gain rating points against generally higher-rated opposition. Her live rating has risen above 2400 during the event.

title: Emin Ohanyan and Jiang Haochen outperform rating favourites, top final standings at Atyrau Masters
summary:
No easy rivals for the top seeds

Armenian GM Emin Ohanyan won the Atyrau Masters in Kazakhstan after finishing tied for first place with Chinese IM Jiang Haochen. Both players scored 7/9, with Ohanyan taking the title thanks to a superior Buchholz tiebreak score. The two young players, seeded 20 th and 30 th respectively, finished ahead of a field that included a number of established grandmasters rated above 2600.

The tournament took place from 12 to 20 October as the third stage of the Kazakhstan Chess Cup. The nine-round Swiss competition featured 109 players in the Masters section, with a first prize of 9 million Kazakhstani tenge (approximately US$20,000). The event was organised by the Kazakhstan Chess Federation, with games played at a time control of 90 minutes plus a 30-second increment per move.

The starting list was headed by Uzbekistan's Shamsiddin Vokhidov (2649), followed by India's Leon Luke Mendonca (2629), Aditya Mittal (2621) and Pranav Anand (2606). Other prominent participants included Maxim Matlakov (2596), former FIDE World Championship challenger Gata Kamsky (2592), Arkadij Naiditsch (2580) and Baadur Jobava (2572).

The competitive nature of the field became evident in the opening two rounds, when both top seeds suffered defeats against considerably lower-rated opponents . Vokhidov lost to Vietnam's Nguyen Duc Hoa (2405) in round one, while Mendonca was beaten by Armenian IM Sergey Sklokin-Bagiyan (2477) in round two. Neither of the two rating favourites managed to fully recover from these setbacks, as both eventually finished on 5½/9.

The closing ceremony | Photos: Kazakhstan Chess Federation

Two young players share first place

Ohanyan, a 20-year-old Armenian GM rated 2520, had a particularly strong start, collecting five wins and a draw in his first six games. The 20 th seed then drew his remaining three encounters to finish the tournament undefeated, with five victories and four draws.

The Armenian faced only two players from the top ten of the starting list. He drew with eighth seed Baadur Jobava and tenth seed Ivan Zemlyanskii in the final two rounds. His performance was sufficient to retain first place, although he was eventually caught by Jiang.

The 15-year-old Chinese IM, rated 2490 and seeded 30 th , followed a different path to the top. Having fallen behind the early leaders, Jiang finished with three consecutive victories, including a win over seventh seed Arkadij Naiditsch in the penultimate round. In round nine, he defeated Sergei Lobanov to reach 7/9 and join Ohanyan at the top of the standings.

The two players did not face each other during the tournament. Their different routes to the final score also help explain the substantial difference in their Buchholz cut-1 tiebreak scores, which take into account the results achieved by their opponents, excluding the lowest-scoring one. Ohanyan finished with 46 points on this measure, compared with Jiang's 36½, and was therefore declared the tournament winner.

A final group photo with tournament winner Emin Ohanyan standing in the centre | Photo: Kazakhstan Chess Federation

Three players finished half a point behind the joint leaders, all on 6½/9: Georgian grandmaster Baadur Jobava, Russia's Ivan Zemlyanskii and Kazakhstan's Aldiyar Ansat. All three remained undefeated throughout the competition. Jobava, the eighth seed, claimed the bronze medal thanks to his superior Buchholz score.

The tournament featured twelve players rated in the 2550–2650 range, but ended with the top five finishers including three competitors seeded outside the top 15. The results demonstrated the ability of lower-rated participants to compete successfully with the established favourites in open tournaments.

One of the most creative players in the circuit, Baadur Jobava, finished in third place | Photo: Kazakhstan Chess Federation
